scenario: On one operator-reported ESP-Mosaico V1.2 sample, boot kernel #35 in normal multiuser RAM mode and run the opt-in one-shot selected-peer RX observer during a WPA3/SAE profile with PMF required.
expected: The selected BSS passes vendor compatibility checks, SAE and the WPA four-way handshake complete with PMF, and the interface obtains an IP address for data exchange.
observed: A fresh ROM entry loaded firmware, kernel and root, then reached normal multiuser init, getty and root login. The full UART capture recorded the observer candidate, begin, restored and terminal markers once each. The observer setup succeeded (0), with prior promiscuous mode disabled and filter 0x1; teardown returned 0/0/0 and restored the saved state. SAE and association were accepted, profile auth mode was 9, and EmberBSD published RUN with the interface joined and link up. During the first attempt the observer counted 118 management frames from the selected AP. It counted zero data frames that passed successful-RX, FromDS and receiver-address-equals-this-station checks; protected-data, A-MSDU, truncated, LLC and EAPOL counters were also zero. About ten seconds later the vendor reported reason 204; the supplicant moved from Associated to Authentication timed out and locally disconnected. No WPA_COMPLETED, negotiated PMF, IP address, DNS or accepted data exchange was observed. The bounded observer result does not establish whether the AP transmitted frames that were not exposed through this callback/filter path.
limits: One operator-reported V1.2 sample and RAM-only trial; this does not establish another board revision or persistent installation.
The RAM root is identified by role only; its private configuration is not part of this shared record.
Observed times are kernel uptime; the full capture duration is not established. The private capture and its path are not part of this shared record.

The receive observer is opt-in and can affect timing. Its ESP-IDF promiscuous callback and filters only report successful RX frames; the data count additionally requires FromDS direction and receiver address equal to this station. These counters do not establish that the AP sent or did not send frames outside the observer's visibility.

Zero matching downlink data/EAPOL counters do not identify whether frames were absent over the air, filtered by firmware, or unavailable at the callback/API boundary. They do not establish normal-mode EAPOL delivery or a radio defect.
No WPA_COMPLETED, negotiated PMF, IP address, DNS or accepted data exchange was established. WPA2-only authentication, reconnect, roaming and sustained transfer remain unaccepted.
